methods.label: Subtract nested rectangle areas
methods.explanation:
Each one-foot border adds two feet to both dimensions, one foot on each opposite side. Let \(x>0\) be the inner rectangle's length in feet. The three nested rectangles have dimensions
\[
1\times x,\qquad 3\times(x+2),\qquad 5\times(x+4).
\]
Subtracting successive rectangle areas gives the areas of the three separate colored regions, from inside outward:
\[
x,\qquad 3(x+2)-x=2x+6,
\]
\[
5(x+4)-3(x+2)=2x+14.
\]
Since \(x>0\), these areas are in increasing order. Three increasing numbers form an arithmetic progression when the middle number is the average of the other two. Thus
\[
2(2x+6)=x+(2x+14).
\]
Simplifying gives \(4x+12=3x+14\), so \(x=2\). The resulting colored areas are \(2,10,18\) square feet, whose successive differences are both \(8\).

The inner rectangle's length is \(\boxed{2}\) feet, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
